subject: RFP follow-up: European sovereignty, region options and deployment controls
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@acmecorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-10 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial RFP questions - data residency & regional deployment

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As we prepare the formal RFP response for Acme's procurement and security teams I wanted to capture a few specific questions about regional availability and data residency so we can include clear language in the procurement doc:

1) Can you confirm which EU regions Redwood currently operates in for production data-plane hosting and whether logs/backups remain in-region?
2) For customers that require EU-only data residency, what deployment options do you offer (hosted EU-only, dedicated in customer VPC, on-prem/private)? Any constraints or minimum commitments?
3) Is the control plane located outside the EU by default? Can it be hosted in-region or customer-managed for compliance controls?
4) KMS/HSM: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and which cloud KMS providers are validated?
5) Cross-region failover: is automatic failover to non-EU regions opt-in only? How is data replicated for DR?
6) Audit logs & retention: retention periods, export mechanisms, and proof for audits (SOCs/ISO).

We're on a tight deadline for the RFP submission next week. Could you provide a consolidated answer set we can drop into the questionnaire? Also attach any region-mapping or architecture diagrams you can share.

Appreciate it — Tom
Security & Privacy Lead
AcmeCorp

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: DRAFT: Acme RFI answers (data residency & regions)

Rachel — attached is draft v1 of the RFI answers (acme_rfi_answers_v1.docx). Below are the key points pulled out for quick review. Please edit for tone and I'll update the doc.

Summary of responses (high level):
- EU data-plane regions: We operate production data-plane endpoints in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). We also currently offer an EU-only hosting option for customers who require data to remain in EU territories. Backups and operational logs are retained in-region by default for Hosted EU and Dedicated deployments.

- Deployment options:
  * Hosted EU (SaaS): production compute and storage in EU regions.
  * Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools deployed into cloud accounts within an EU region; ensures data-plane and ephemeral caches remain in-region. Minimum commitment: 3-node pool (depends on model/throughput).
  * Redwood Private: VPC or on-prem package where the entire stack (control plane optional) can be deployed in-customer environment.

- Control plane: the default control plane for our hosted offering is currently in a US control region for multi-region orchestration. For customers with strict sovereignty requirements, we support (a) a regional control plane deployment (EU) as part of Private, or (b) a customer-managed control plane in VPC deployments.

- KMS & HSM: BYOK supported. Validated integrations: AWS KMS, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS. We also support remote HSM via PKCS#11 for enterprise HSM appliances. Customer-managed key lifecycle actions (rotate/revoke) are logged in audit trails.

- Cross-region failover & replication:
  * Failover to a non-EU region is opt-in for customers requiring strict EU-only residency.
  * For Hosted EU, we offer same-region failover and optional cross-region DR (replication snapshot exports encrypted with customer key). Replication only occurs when customer opts in and is documented in the SLA.

- Audit logs & retention:
  * Access & admin audit logs: retained for 365 days by default for Hosted and Dedicated (configurable).
  * Data-plane request logs (token-level) are retained for 90 days; can be exported to customer Storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) for longer retention.
  * We can provide signed Audit packages for SOC2/ISO requests and scripted evidence extracts for third-party auditors.

- Data deletion & egress:
  * Customer data deletion requests are executed within 48 hours for hosted accounts; complete purge from backups within 30 days (subject to backup window). Private deployments follow customer policies.

Open items for Acme (we recommend explicit acceptance in MSA):
- Whether Acme requires control plane to be EU-hosted or customer-managed.
- Desired backup retention beyond defaults.
- Acceptance of opt-in cross-region DR (if they require automatic failover to non-EU regions we will need a written exception).

I'll refine the language for the RFP annex and produce a concise PDF you can attach to procurement.

-Neha
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-11 12:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: European sovereignty, region options and deployment controls

Tom — attaching the consolidated response set (Acme_RFI_Answers_20260511.pdf) and the region mapping index. Key points below (extracted from Neha's draft):

1) EU production regions and in-region retention:
- Data plane (production compute + persistent storage): eu-west-1 (Ireland), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For customers that opt into Hosted EU, all data-plane compute, storage, backups and operational logs are kept in the EU by default.

2) Deployment options for EU-only residency:
- Hosted EU: SaaS endpoints that ensure compute + storage in EU regions. Good for teams that want low setup time.
- Dedicated: Reserved capacity deployed into cloud accounts in your selected EU region; ensures logical separation and in-region residency. Typical minimum capacity and lead time depend on model family and throughput; sample commitment is a 3-node pool with a 4–6 week lead time for provisioning.
- Private: Full VPC or on-prem installation that can be deployed entirely inside your network and region. Control plane can be customer-managed.

3) Control plane and sovereignty:
- Default hosted control plane: multi-region orchestration services reside in our control region.
- Options for sovereignty: for enterprise customers we offer a regional control-plane deployment (EU) as part of Redwood Private, and a customer-managed control plane option in VPC deployments. We will document control-plane location in the MSA.

4) KMS, BYOK, HSM:
- Supported: AWS KMS, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, and PKCS#11-compatible HSM appliances.
- Customer-managed keys: supported for encryption-at-rest and backup encryption; key usage and rotation operations are recorded to audit logs.

5) Cross-region DR & failover:
- Cross-region replication is opt-in. Automatic failover to non-EU regions will not occur unless explicitly enabled and signed in the agreement.

6) Auditing & evidence:
- SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 attestations available (redacted reports available under NDA). Audit logs exportable and retention adjustable per contract.

7) Deletion and retention windows:
- Hosted deletion: account-level deletion processed within 48 hours; backups purged within 30 days.

Please review the attached PDF for ready-to-drop text for your RFP questionnaire. If Acme's legal requires stronger contractual guarantees around control-plane location or per-country residency (e.g., Germany-only), we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) and we'll engage Solutions + Legal to add an SLA clause.

Next steps: let me know if you want us to add a short SLA paragraph on region-specific retention and control-plane location; Karthik can provide a short paragraph on provisioning times and minimum pool sizes.

Thanks — Rachel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: European sovereignty, region options and deployment controls

Tom — quick answers to your clarifications: 

1) Immutable snapshots/backups: Immutable snapshots retained for DR are considered part of backup retention; if you select a 30-day purge window that applies to standard backups. For long-term immutable DR snapshots we can set a separate retention policy (e.g., 90/180 days) and encrypt them with your BYOK. This will be documented as an opt-in in the SLA.

2) Germany-only: Dedicated can be provisioned in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) which meets Germany-only residency for data-plane and backups. If you require guaranteed control-plane locality within Germany (not just data-plane), we recommend Redwood Private or a regional control-plane deployment as part of our Private offering — we'll engage Legal for a region-binding MSA clause.

I'll loop Solutions Engineering and Legal to prepare the SLA language and an MSA addendum we can attach to your RFP. Expect a short update tomorrow morning.

Best — Rachel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
